newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer in slow re-opening.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer in slow re-opening.

text.p: Precious metals were mixed in a slow start to post-Christmas trade on Friday morning with gold and silver a touch up and platinum just easier, dealers said.
"Anything that is happening is just back-to-back business and a few final positions being cleared up before year end," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $369.55 per ounce up from $368.90 on Tuesday morning before the two-day Christmas break.
Business had been very slow in New York on Thursday but modest gains were held in quiet Far East markets.
Dealers said there was light lending through the year end but short dates were barely profitable.
The Comex option expiry for gold and silver at the close of business in New York was expected to have little impact on the spot market, dealers said.
Activity next week was forecast to remain light given the New Year holdiay in Europe and the United States on Wednesday and a series of holidays closing the Tokyo markets all week.
"It will be the first week in January before we see anything like a return to normal. Until then gold should remain in a one-dollar range," a dealer said.

Silver was marked up about four cents from Tuesday to $4.88/$4.90 reflecting a little position squaring which was proferred as the main reason for the sparse activity in the other white metals where there was no fresh news.
Platinum was about $1.50 below Tuesday's close at $370.50/$371.50 and palladium was unchanged at $116.75/$117.75.
